messages.subject: Part 4 sleep efficiency
parts:
Dear Vincent,

I wanted to use  the following code  to calculate the sleep-related parameters, and we used GENEActiv to measure 7 days (100 HZ) circadian rhythm.

g.shell.GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
                      datadir="D:/......bin",
                      outputdir="C:/......",
                      studyname = ".......",
                      do.report=c(2,4,5),
                     
                      #part2#
                      strategy = 1,
                      hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
                      maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
                      qwindow=c(0,24),
                      mvpathreshold =c(100),
                      bout.metric = 4,
                      excludefirstlast = FALSE,
                      includenightcrit = 16,
                     
                      #part3 and 4#
                      def.noc.sleep = 1,
                      outliers.only = TRUE,
                      criterror = 4,
                      do.visual = TRUE,
                      ignorenonwear=T,
                     
                      #part 5#
                      threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
                      boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
                      boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
                      boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
                      includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,
                     
                      #visual report#
                      timewindow = c("WW"),
                      visualreport=TRUE)

However,  I could not find sleep efficiency in the part 4 report. Could you please help me check the code? 
Thank you!

Best regards,
Gengze

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: Part 4 sleep efficiency
parts:
Hi Gengze,

Sleep efficiency isn't calculated within GGIR unless you have used a sleep log or when using guider HorAngle for hip-worn accelerometer data. If either of these applies set argument sleepwindowType to “TimeInBed”. See this info in section 4.2.1.1 in the vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html 

Alternatively, you can just calculate this yourself in the nightsummary.csv as: 
Sleepefficiency = SleepDurationInSpt /  SptDuration 

Kind regards,
Ben

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Part 4 sleep efficiency
parts:
Thanks Ben for jumping in.

Just wanted to clarify that:

sleep_efficiency = SleepDurationInSpt/SptDuration
​
is not entirely in line with how the sleep research community defines sleep efficiency. The official definition is to also include sleep latency. However, because we do not have sleep latency in many GGIR applications (without sleep log that asks the person when they went to bed) you could argue that the above calculation is at least some attempt to quantify sleep efficiency. However, be aware that the values will differ between both definitions and report that this is how it is calculated.

In earlier version of GGIR I used this definition of sleep efficiency in GGIR part4 output. When I became aware of the inconsistency with what sleep researchers do, I removed it from part4 output which now only shows sleep efficiency if sleep latency is known.

I believe the latency-free sleep efficiency is still part of part 5 output,  so in that sense I have not been entirely consistent.

In other words, part 4 output is an attempt to align with terminology and definitions of sleep research, while part 5 output is more aimed at a general audience interested in 24 hour time use. 

Best, Vincent
